summary: The Legion extension for Oh My Pi now delivers a phase worker's one-time credential (LEGION_GRANT) through the bash tool's per-command `env` instead of prepending it to the command text. The cause the planner measured is confirmed by the instrumented hook on both rig legs: the hook mints exactly one grant per bash call, and every extra credential line was text the model wrote after Oh My Pi wrote the hook's revised input back into its message. On the fixed code every rig check passes in both legs; on the unfixed code both legs reproduce the 403.
rebase: Rebased legion/LEGION-12 onto main@origin at e01661365b2b (`chore: release pi-envoy v1.8.1`). LEGION-16 (pull request #961, 'Controller runs as an attachable TUI session and owns the merge queue') had not merged, so the change lands against main's shape: the single worker hook in packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts. When LEGION-16 rebases onto this, its unified `wrap(grant)` helper must put `workerGhEnvironment(...)` into `env` (hook keys spread last) rather than joining it into `command`; the architect coordinates that order.

packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/gh-shim.ts — `workerGhEnvironment(grantId, stateDir, workerBin, basePath)` returns an env record (LEGION_GRANT, GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_HOST cleared to '', GH_CONFIG_DIR, PATH = workerBin + delimiter + basePath) instead of shell text; `shellLiteral` stays for the shim script.

The profile's bash interceptor blocks `… > file` redirections with 'use the write tool'; the unfixed code masked this because the prelude text preceded the command. The rig's credential step therefore writes to stdout.

Inside a Legion pane the pi-envoy test fixture used to restore the pane's own LEGION_BOOT_TOKEN_FILE after every test, so `recovers a live worker's capability…` booted with the pane's uuid boot token and asserted the wrong recoveryToken. The fixture's baseline is now 'not a Legion pane' (same remedy #967 applied to the daemon CLI tests).

`legion gh` spawns `gh` with the worker shim still first on PATH, so the shim runs `legion gh` a second time and the grant is redeemed twice per `legion gh` call (both 200; a live grant is re-redeemable). Harmless, one extra daemon round-trip; a fast-follow could strip the shim directory in `buildGitHubTokenEnv`.

An imitated credential line in command text, if a model still writes one (a session resumed from a pre-fix transcript), is executed by the shell and overrides the env value for that one command; the fix removes the seed for fresh sessions, it cannot rewrite what an old transcript already shows. Stated in the doc caveat.

This implementer session had the bug itself: one push 403'd because the model wrote imitated credential lines; the retry with a clean command pushed. Recorded because the plan asked for it, and because it is the same signature the rig measured.

pullRequestDraft.title: fix(pi-envoy): deliver the worker's one-time credential through the shell tool's environment, not the command text
pullRequestDraft.body:
Dispatch: LEGION-12

## What was wrong

Every Legion phase worker runs its shell commands through a hook in the Legion extension for Oh My Pi (`packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts`). For each command the hook mints a one-time credential from the Legion daemon (the `LEGION_GRANT` variable, valid for 60 seconds) so the command can push code, call GitHub through `legion gh`, and report its phase with `legion handoff complete`. Until now the hook delivered that credential by prepending a block of shell text to the command.

Oh My Pi writes a hook's revised tool input back into the model's own message. The credential block therefore appeared in the transcript as text the model had written. On later commands the model read its own transcript and copied the block, with placeholder, made-up, or stale ids. The hook's real block was always first, the imitations followed, and a shell keeps the last `export`, so the command ran under an id the daemon had never issued and got a 403. The count grew as the session filled with examples, which is why pushes, GitHub calls, and phase reports failed more and more as a session went on.

The hook itself never multiplied. With one debug line per hook invocation added in this change, a headless worker driven through 31 shell commands and three `task` spawns against a stand-in daemon showed exactly one hook invocation and one credential minted per command, while the credential lines in the command text climbed 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, … up to 7, every extra one an id the stand-in never issued. An interactive terminal session showed the same.

## What changes

- The credential now travels in the bash tool's per-command `env` argument, which Oh My Pi applies to that one command only and never writes into command text. The same `env` carries the cleared `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GH_HOST`, the isolated `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, and a `PATH` with the worker's `gh` shim first (built on the pane's own `PATH`, never the model's).
- The hook's keys are spread last, so a model that imitates a previous command's `env` object cannot displace the credential minted for the current command. The command text is not inspected or rewritten.
- `workerGhEnvironment` (in `packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/gh-shim.ts`, the builder of that per-command environment) returns the env record instead of shell text.
- Two permanent debug log lines make this measurable: an instance id on `extension instance loaded`, and one `legion tool_call hook` line per invocation.
- Two regression tests in `packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.test.ts` fail on `main` and pass here: one proves the credential reaches `env` with `command` untouched and exactly one mint per call, even when the model supplied its own stale `env`; the other proves re-feeding the same tool call with its already-revised input still yields one credential and no growth in `PATH`. The test fixture now starts from a non-Legion environment, so the suite passes from inside a Legion worker pane.
- A proof rig under `packages/pi-envoy/scripts/grant-rig/` (a stand-in daemon with the real request shapes and the real 60-second, repeatedly-redeemable credential rule; a driver for the headless and the terminal leg; a shared analyzer) reproduces the failure on the unfixed code and passes on this branch.
- `docs/solutions/legion/worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md` section 1 records the cause and retires the shell workaround.

Not changed: the daemon's credential rules, the `legion` command-line tool, and the Oh My Pi fork.

## Verification

**CI:** `pr-checks-result` run <run id> — <result> at <head sha>. (Filled in when the pull request opens.)

**Threads:** 0 resolved, 0 unresolved.

**Thermo:** left for the reviewer.

**E2E:** left for the tester. Implementer's own run, to be replaced: the grant rig (`packages/pi-envoy/scripts/grant-rig/README.md`) on the unfixed code, headless leg — 31 shell commands, 31 credentials minted, one hook invocation per command, credential lines in the command text 1→7, `legion credential get`, `legion gh -- --version`, and `legion handoff complete` all `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)`; on this branch, same leg — 31 commands, 31 credentials, zero credential lines in any command text, `env.LEGION_GRANT` equal to the credential minted for every command, every redemption 200, those three commands `exit=0` on commands 27–31. Terminal leg through `tmux -L l12rig`: 8 commands, same result on both codes. Negative control: a credential the stand-in never issued → `Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT (403)`.

**Fast-follow:** `bunx biome format --write packages/pi-envoy/extensions/envoy.test.ts packages/pi-envoy/tsconfig.json` (formatter drift already on `main`, not touched here), and stripping the worker shim directory from the `PATH` that `legion gh` hands to `gh` (`buildGitHubTokenEnv` in `packages/daemon/src/daemon/github-app-env.ts`) so one `legion gh` call redeems its credential once instead of twice.

**Chain:** not stacked.
